name: obey-architecture-decision

files.README.md:
# feedhub

feedhub polls podcast RSS feeds, normalises them, and serves one merged episode
catalogue to the mobile clients.

## Layout

- src/http - the shared client and the per-integration base URL registry.
- src/feeds - feed parsing, deduplication, and the refresh scheduler.

## Running locally

    npm install
    npm run build
    npm test

history.task: Deduplicate episodes when a feed rewrites its guids on every publish
history.summary: One network rewrites every episode guid each time it republishes a feed, so the catalogue grew a duplicate row per refresh. Episode identity is now the enclosure url plus the published date rather than the guid, and the duplicate rows already in the catalogue were collapsed by a one-off backfill.

tests.summary: 22 parser cases pass, including the guid-rewrite regression

history.task: Consolidate the three hand-rolled fetch call sites that talk to podcast hosts
history.summary: The iTunes lookup, the Megaphone feed pull, and the artwork download each carried their own fetch call, their own timeout, and their own idea of what a retry means. All three now go through src/http/adapter.ts. Every outbound HTTP call goes through HttpAdapter from here on, so that retry, timeout, and rate-limit handling stays in one place instead of being reinvented once per integration. src/http/registry.ts maps an integration name to its base URL and its rate budget, so wiring up a new provider is one registration line and no new networking code.
decisions: Every outbound HTTP call goes through HttpAdapter. A direct fetch or undici call outside src/http is a review blocker, because retry, timeout, and rate-limit handling stays in one place there and nowhere else.
An integration that needs more than three retries is moved to the background queue rather than retrying inline, so a slow provider cannot pin a request thread.

tests.summary: adapter and registry cases pass, including the 429 backoff case

history.task: Warm the artwork cache overnight so the 9am spike stops timing out
history.summary: A nightly job now walks the top 500 shows and pulls their artwork ahead of the morning traffic spike, which removed the 9am latency shoulder on the catalogue endpoint. The warm-up is spaced at five requests a second so it does not starve live traffic.

history.task: Investigate why one network's episode descriptions arrive empty
history.summary: That network serves descriptions only to clients that send a signed partner header, and we do not have credentials for it yet. There is nothing to change on our side until the partner agreement lands, so the regression stays red and quarantined.

history.task: Write the feed refresh cadence into the readme
history.summary: Wrote the refresh cadence into the readme - hourly for subscribed shows, daily for the long tail - so a support engineer can answer the where-is-my-episode question without reading the scheduler code.

# feedhub

feedhub polls podcast RSS feeds, normalises them, and serves one merged episode
catalogue to the mobile clients.

## Layout

- src/http - the shared client and the per-integration base URL registry.
- src/feeds - feed parsing, deduplication, and the refresh scheduler.

## Running locally

    npm install
    npm run build
    npm test

## Refresh cadence

Subscribed shows are refreshed hourly. Everything else is refreshed once a day,
shortly after midnight UTC. A show promoted into the subscribed set is refreshed
on the next hourly tick rather than immediately.

history.task: Speed up the merged catalogue endpoint for very large libraries
history.summary: The catalogue endpoint built its response by repeatedly concatenating arrays; it now streams episodes in published order. The p95 for a 20k-episode library dropped from 1.8s to 240ms and the allocation count fell by an order of magnitude.

query: We are adding a Spotify catalog integration that needs to download episode artwork over the network. Where should the outgoing request code live?

allOf: every outbound HTTP call goes through HttpAdapter
retry, timeout, and rate-limit handling stays in one place
more than three retries is moved to the background queue
